title: Path resolver
description: Type an absolute or relative path with `.`, `..`, `~` or `~jonas` from any current directory and watch it resolve to one absolute path, step by step.
intro: Pick `/home/mira/studio` as the current directory and type `pixel-raiders/assets`. Then type `builds/..`, then `/tmp`, then `~jonas`. Notice that only the first two depend on where you are. Finally, try `~/studio/./builds/../pixel-raiders` and count how many steps do nothing useful.
takeaways: An absolute path starts with `/` and means the same thing from every directory. A relative path does not start with `/` and is read from the current directory, which `pwd` prints.
`.` is the current directory and `..` is its parent. At the root, `..` is still `/`, because the root is its own parent. `cd ..` goes up one level.

The shell, not the command, expands `~` to your home directory (`/home/mira` for Mira) and `~jonas` to Jonas's home. A `~` in the middle of a word is just a character, and `~` followed by an unknown name stays as typed.
`cd` with no argument, `cd ~` and `cd $HOME` all take you home; `cd -` jumps back to the previous directory.
Doubled slashes and a trailing slash change nothing: `/home//mira/` is `/home/mira`. Names are case-sensitive, so `Studio` and `studio` are two different directories.

A path to something that does not exist is still a valid path. It fails only when a command tries to use it, with "No such file or directory", or "Not a directory" when a file stands where a directory should be.

tasks.text: Mira is in `sprites`, deep inside the game project. Give a relative path to the `builds` folder next to `pixel-raiders`.
tasks.why: Each `..` climbs one level: sprites to assets, to pixel-raiders, to studio. Then `builds` goes down. `../../../builds` works.

tasks.text: Mira is in `/tmp` and wants to reach Jonas's home directory. Use the tilde form.
tasks.why: `~jonas` is replaced by the shell with Jonas's home directory, wherever you are.

tasks.text: Mira is in `/etc` and wants her own `notes.txt` from the project folder. Use an absolute path.
tasks.why: An absolute path starts at `/` and ignores the current directory: `/home/mira/studio/pixel-raiders/notes.txt`.

tasks.text: Mira is in `studio`. Give the shortest relative path to her home directory.
tasks.why: `..` is the parent of `studio`, which is her home. `cd ..` would take her there.

tasks.text: Mira is in `builds`. Give a relative path to `assets` inside the `pixel-raiders` folder.
tasks.why: Go up to `studio` with `..`, then down through `pixel-raiders` into `assets`: `../pixel-raiders/assets`.

tasks.text: Mira is in `pixel-raiders`. Use the tilde and `studio` to reach the `builds` folder.
tasks.why: `~` is `/home/mira`, so `~/studio/builds` always works, wherever she is.
